corpus.notes: The PINNED corpus these budgets were measured on, enforced by check_budgets.assert_corpus_shape and mirrored by harness.DEFAULT_CORPUS. It names two job directories, not the directory research/evidence/runs, because three of the six profiled paths ('ingest', 'projection', 'facts') take the loaded job list and so scale with however much evidence happens to be committed. Promoting evidence must not move this gate. A report whose corpus_roots/corpus_jobs/corpus_result_json differ from this block is not measuring what these budgets describe and MUST NOT be cited as a re-baseline sample. Changing the pin means re-baselining and updating this block in the same commit.

notes: CI-local ceilings in milliseconds of median after warmup+5 reps on the committed 2-job evidence corpus. tolerance_pct=50; ceiling = budget * 1.5. PROVENANCE IS MIXED. CI-runner-anchored: 'ingest' was re-baselined 2026-08-15 from the ingest medians of the last 14 successful perf runs on ubuntu-latest with the postgres service container (n=14, 51.4-96.1 ms, median 72.3 ms), plus one 125.2 ms runner-variance spike on a commit that passed on rerun; 115.0 is ~1.2x the observed successful max and its 172.5 ms ceiling is ~1.38x that spike. Laptop-anchored (NOT re-measured on CI): 'digest' and 'queue-tick-100' are still about 3x the 2026-08-14 SPEED capture on an Apple Silicon laptop with a local PostgreSQL, so their true CI headroom is unknown; 'fleet-status' is git/gh-bound rather than machine-class-anchored. Any future re-baseline must cite CI artifact samples, not a single laptop timing. An improvement below 50% of a budget should re-baseline. CORPUS PIN (2026-08-16): the profiled default is now the two job directories named in 'corpus' above rather than the directory research/evidence/runs. No budget value and no tolerance changed: the pinned set is exactly the 2-job corpus every number above was already measured on, so pinning preserves their meaning instead of resetting it. Confirmed by three local runs on 2026-08-16 (macOS-26.5-arm64, Python 3.12.11, scratch Postgres evallab_speed_prof, median of 5 reps after 1 warmup each): ingest 28.638/30.390/31.198, projection 2.811/2.884/3.187, facts 3.861/3.905/4.048, digest 0.876/0.927/0.964, queue-tick-100 74.679/74.837/78.202, fleet-status 2234.392/2240.928/2250.273 ms - every median inside its ceiling. CI RE-BASELINE OF 'projection' AND 'facts' (2026-10-29, NP23-CE-1): both paths publish every table with one durable replace (16 and 24 fsyncs per rep on this corpus), so on shared runners their medians measured the runner's disk, not the code. 18 runs of unchanged code (origin/main 522d55257, workflow_dispatch, one run per probe branch) gave projection 4.9-225.5 ms (median 7.5) and facts 11.6-104.5 ms (median 16.1); 5 of the 18 runs failed a budget (path failures: projection 3, facts 2, queue-tick-100 1; one run failed two paths). 42 runs with the profile scratch directory on tmpfs (--scratch-dir /dev/shm/evallab-speed, now what perf.yml passes) gave projection 0.9-3.2 ms (median 1.7) and facts 4.0-9.6 ms (median 6.5) and no failure, the same order as the 2026-08-14 laptop capture (2.7 and 3.5 ms). projection 25.0 -> 4.0 (ceiling 6.0) and facts 25.0 -> 12.0 (ceiling 18.0) are about 1.9x the observed CI maximum and 3.5x / 2.8x the observed median; against those medians the old 37.5 ms ceilings allowed 22x and 5.8x. The facts medians are bimodal (about 4.0-5.8 ms and 7.3-9.6 ms, two runner CPU pools), the upper pool sits at 80% of the budget, and 42 samples cannot rule out a third, slower pool. The advisory 'under 50% of budget' notice will print for 'projection' and for the faster facts pool: these budgets are sized to the observed maximum, not to 3x the median. WHAT THE GATE NO LONGER TIMES: the runner's disk (fsync and file-creation latency, not separated from each other: queue-tick-100 does no fsync and still failed once in 18 on disk). The sync-write cost those paths used to include is pinned instead by tests/test_profile_harness.py: one durable replace (two fsyncs) per published table and no fsync per lease in a queue tick. 'ingest' still writes through the Postgres service's disk. Local runs: macOS fsync is cheap and passes; on Linux pass --scratch-dir /dev/shm/<dir> before check_budgets.py.
